newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin lauches retooled debt agency.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin lauches retooled debt agency.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Thursday launched a retooled government agency designed to boost sales of Canada Savings Bonds and other retail debt products.
Martin also said the government will be making changes to the 50-year old Canada Saving Bonds program, including extending the length of time the bonds pay a guaranteed minimum interest rate.
The finance minister said the changes are being made to halt a decline since 1987 in sales of Canada Savings Bonds, which are sold to individuals and are not traded.

The agency now administering sales of retail debt will be know as Canada Investment and Savings. The agency was formed last year as the Canada Retail Debt Agency with the goal of boosting retail debt product sales.

Among the changes being considered for the Canada Savings Bond program are pricing the bonds to carry a minimum guaranteed interest rate for up to a decade. The bonds now carry a guaranteed rate for a maximum of three years.
The agency is also lauching a pilot program with some companies to reduce the workload involved in offering Canada Savings Bonds to employees through payroll savings.

Canada Investment and Savings will also be reducing administration demands on financial institutions for Canada Savings Bonds sales of less than C$1,000, said Martin. A pilot program will also be established to make sales of less than C$1000 of the bonds available through some post offices.
Martin said the bonds, which are held by about seven million Canadians and account for about C$30 billion of the national debt, represent "a special anchor" in turbulent global financial markets.
This year Canada Savings Bonds go on sale from Tuesday October 15 until Friday, November 1.
